Why ChatGPT Describes Your Startup Wrong (and How to Fix It)

ChatGPT has wrong or outdated facts about your company? 2026 data on what AI gets wrong about B2B brands, where the errors come from, and a step-by-step fix list.

By Anupam Varshney, Founder, Octaloop

Short answer: ChatGPT usually gets your company wrong because it has too little clear, consistent public information to work from, so it fills the gaps from memory or stretches a loose claim on your own site. You can't edit its answers, but you can change what it reads: publish your key facts in plain text on a dated page, make your profiles and schema agree, correct the third-party pages it leans on, and earn fresh coverage, then re-check every month.

If you've asked ChatGPT about your own startup and winced at the answer, you're in a big club. In a July 2026 study where 1,704 brands graded the facts AI engines stated about them, three in four brands that checked at least 20 facts found at least one that was false (Searchable, July 2026). This guide explains where the wrong facts come from and gives you a fix list in the order that actually works.

How often does ChatGPT get companies wrong?

Often enough that you should assume it's happening to you until you've checked. Three independent 2026 studies measured it in different ways:

Study What was measured Headline finding
Searchable, July 2026 32,556 AI-stated facts, each graded by an employee of the brand 9.2% flagged false overall; ChatGPT 8.1%, Google AI Overviews 11.4%, Perplexity 11.5%. Small firms (50 staff or fewer) saw 9.4% vs 6.3% for large firms
Resonance, September 2026 Almost 50,000 answers about 116 B2B tech companies, checked against verified fact packs ChatGPT had at least one error in 49% of answers and a serious error in about 1 in 20; Perplexity 63%, Gemini 83%
Broadcastwell, October 2026 2,922 statements about 70 leading software vendors across five engines, checked against each vendor's own pages 5.8% of verifiable statements were wrong or stale, but 880 statements (about 30%) couldn't be verified at all from the vendors' own pages

The numbers differ because the methods differ. Broadcastwell looked at the five most-named vendors in each category, which are the best-documented companies on the web. Searchable and Resonance included smaller firms. The pattern across all three is the same: the less clearly a company is documented, the more the AI guesses. Searchable found AI and machine-learning companies had the highest false-fact rate of any sector, at 18.5%, and SaaS sat at 9.5%.

Why it matters: in G2's March 2026 survey of 1,076 B2B software buyers, 51% said they now start software research in an AI chatbot more often than in Google (G2, April 2026). A wrong price or a missing integration can knock you off a shortlist before anyone visits your site, and nobody files a complaint about it. They just pick someone else.

What does ChatGPT usually get wrong?

The errors cluster around facts that change often or that buyers ask about precisely.

Fact type How often it was wrong (Searchable, July 2026) What it looks like for a SaaS company
Pricing 13.5% (16.1% for US brands) An old plan price, a free tier you removed, "contact sales" turned into an invented number
Funding and financials 10.9% A round you never raised, an old valuation, wrong headcount
Integrations and tech stack 10.6% "Doesn't integrate with Salesforce" when it does
Partnerships and clients 9.9% A logo you never worked with, a partner from three years ago
Products and services 8.6% Your old category, a sunset product, a feature you never built
History and founding 6.9% Wrong founder, founding year or HQ

Resonance's analysis adds two important details. First, in 57% of all errors the assistant added specific details the company had never published, usually because a buyer asked a precise question that no public page answered. Second, the average answer left out four or five verified facts, more than twice the number of errors. So "the AI doesn't mention our enterprise plan" is as common a problem as "the AI got our price wrong," and it's harder to notice.

Where do the wrong facts come from?

This is the part most fix-it guides skip, and it decides what you do next. A wrong answer comes from one of three places:

  1. Memory (training data). The model learned something about you, or about a company with a similar name, and repeats it. Resonance found about two thirds of errors across all assistants had no source behind them (61% for ChatGPT), which points to memory. These are the slowest to change, because they depend on the wider web describing you consistently over months.
  2. Your own pages. Your site, stretched. Resonance traced 27% of ChatGPT's errors to the company's own pages: an old pricing page still indexed, a vague "works with all major CRMs," a case study figure quoted without context. These are the fastest to fix.
  3. Third-party pages. A directory listing, an old article, a review profile, a competitor's comparison page. These caused fewer errors (6% of ChatGPT's in Resonance's data), but they did more damage: 15% of third-party-sourced errors were rated serious, against 7% from companies' own pages.

The difference between memory and live retrieval also explains why engines disagree. Perplexity and ChatGPT search pull live pages for many questions, so a fix on a cited page can show up quickly. Answers built from training data move slowly. We cover how the engines differ in more depth in AEO vs GEO vs SEO.

How do you diagnose what ChatGPT says about you?

Spend an afternoon on this before changing anything. Spot checks mislead: Searchable notes that brands checking only two or three facts often find nothing wrong.

  1. Write your fact sheet first. One page, internal, with the 15 to 25 facts you'd want every buyer to know: what you do in one sentence, category, pricing approach, plans, key integrations, certifications, data residency, founders, founding year, HQ, funding, notable customers you're allowed to name.
  2. Ask the questions buyers ask. Use 15 to 20 prompts across three types:
    • Branded: "What does [Company] do?", "How much does [Company] cost?", "Does [Company] integrate with HubSpot?", "Is [Company] SOC 2 compliant?"
    • Comparison: "[Company] vs [Competitor]", "Alternatives to [Competitor]"
    • Category: "Best [category] tools for startups"
  3. Run them on ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews or AI Mode, and Gemini. Answers vary between runs, so run each prompt at least twice and note anything that repeats. Resonance found about one error in ten came back in later answers, and those repeat errors are the ones to chase first.
  4. Log every error and every gap against your fact sheet, plus any source the engine cites for it.
  5. Tag each error by likely origin: cited your page, cited a third-party page, or no source (memory).

You now have a list that tells you exactly which fix applies to which error.

How do you fix what ChatGPT says about your company?

We use what we call an Entity Fact Sheet approach: one source of truth for your company, published in public, mirrored everywhere the engines look, and checked on a schedule. Work through it in this order, fastest lever first.

1. Publish the facts buyers ask about, in plain text, on a dated page

Most errors fill a gap, so close the gap. Put your pricing approach, plans, integrations, certifications and data residency on crawlable HTML pages, with a visible "last updated" date. If you don't publish prices, say so plainly ("Pricing is custom and starts after a scoping call") so the engine has something true to quote instead of a guess. Add a short "About [Company]: key facts" block to your About page that mirrors your fact sheet.

2. Clean up your own site

Read your pages the way an assistant would. Remove or redirect old pricing pages and sunset product pages. Replace loose claims ("integrates with everything") with specific lists. Give every number context: who, when, and measured how. This is the one source you control completely, and it causes more of ChatGPT's errors than any third-party page.

3. Let the engines read your site

Check that your robots.txt doesn't block the crawlers that power AI search. OpenAI says sites must not block OAI-SearchBot to appear in ChatGPT search answers, and that robots.txt changes take about 24 hours to apply (OpenAI, crawler overview). Key facts should be in the HTML, not loaded by JavaScript or locked in PDFs.

4. Make your schema and profiles agree

Add Organization schema with your legal name, description, founding date, founders, logo and sameAs links to your official LinkedIn, Crunchbase, G2 and social profiles. Then update those profiles so the name, one-line description, category, HQ and founding year match your fact sheet word for word. Schema won't get you recommended on its own, but its real job is getting you described correctly: it tells the engine which entity is you. Searchable calls schema and consistent profiles the fastest lever available, and contradictions between sources are what produce wrong answers.

5. Claim your Wikidata entry and Google Knowledge Panel

A Wikidata item has a lower bar than Wikipedia and is machine-readable; Searchable lists it as a high-leverage, under-used step. If Google shows a Knowledge Panel for your company, an official representative can claim it and submit verified "Suggest edits" requests with supporting public URLs; Google says it reviews verified feedback within a few days (Google Knowledge Panel Help).

6. Correct the third-party pages with the most reach

Start with the pages the engines actually cited in your diagnosis. Update review sites and directories you control (G2, Capterra, Crunchbase, LinkedIn). For articles with outdated facts, email the editor with the specific correction and a public source. Ask partners and integration marketplaces to fix stale listings.

7. Earn fresh, accurate coverage

This is what eventually changes the model's memory. New, independent articles that state your current positioning give every engine a better source to cite and, over time, retrain on. Our guide to digital PR for AEO covers how to find the publications engines already cite for your category, and our piece on events and conferences for AEO shows how one talk can produce five accurate, citable pages.

8. Use feedback buttons, but don't rely on them

You can flag a bad answer with the thumbs-down in ChatGPT or Gemini. It costs nothing, but there's no public evidence it fixes a fact about a company. Treat it as a bonus, not the plan.

How long does it take for ChatGPT to update information about you?

It depends on where the error came from.

Error origin What fixes it Typical time to see a change
Your own page, cited live Edit or remove the page Days to a few weeks on engines that search live; OpenAI notes ~24 hours for robots.txt changes to take effect
Third-party page, cited live Correction from the publisher or profile owner Weeks, depending on how fast they update
Memory (no source) Consistent facts across many sources, plus new coverage Months, and often only after a model update

That's why the re-check cadence matters. Resonance recommends checking monthly and judging progress over a quarter, which matches our experience: live-search answers move first, memory-based answers last.

What doesn't fix AI misinformation?

  • Publishing a single "correction" page and stopping. One page can't outvote ten old ones.
  • An llms.txt file on its own. It's reasonable hygiene, but no major engine has said it uses it to decide company facts.
  • Stuffing schema with claims your pages don't support. Schema should mirror visible content, not replace it.
  • Arguing with the chatbot. Telling ChatGPT it's wrong in a chat changes nothing for the next buyer.
  • Checking once. Answers change as models and sources change; Resonance saw ChatGPT's factual score move between April and September 2026.

Should you fix this yourself or get help?

A founder can do steps 1 to 6 in a couple of focused weeks: write the fact sheet, clean the site, fix schema and profiles, and send corrections. What's harder in-house is the ongoing part: running a fixed prompt set across four engines every month, tracing each repeat error to its source, and earning the new coverage that shifts what the models remember.

When you compare agencies, ask whether they'll show you the error log by engine and by source, not just a visibility score, and whether they can actually earn press, not only publish on your blog. Fixing how AI describes you is mostly a PR problem with a technical layer on top.

FAQ

Why does ChatGPT have wrong information about my company?

Usually because there's too little clear, consistent public information about you. Resonance's September 2026 study found about two thirds of AI errors about B2B companies had no source behind them, meaning the model filled gaps from memory, and 27% of ChatGPT's errors traced back to the company's own pages being stretched.

How often does ChatGPT get company facts wrong?

In Searchable's July 2026 study, brands flagged 8.1% of ChatGPT's facts about them as false, and three in four brands that checked 20 or more facts found at least one false fact. Resonance found ChatGPT made at least one error in 49% of answers about B2B tech companies.

Can I contact OpenAI to correct what ChatGPT says about my company?

There's no public process for companies to edit ChatGPT's answers. You change what it reads instead: your own site, your profiles and schema, third-party pages, and fresh coverage. Make sure your site doesn't block OAI-SearchBot so ChatGPT search can read your corrections.

What facts does AI get wrong most often about brands?

Pricing (13.5% false), funding and financials (10.9%) and integrations (10.6%), according to Searchable's July 2026 data. These change often, so publish them on dated pages and keep them current.

Does schema markup fix wrong AI answers?

It helps the engines identify which entity is you and link your official profiles through sameAs, which reduces mix-ups. It won't overturn errors that many other pages repeat, so pair it with site clean-up, profile consistency and third-party corrections.

How long does it take for ChatGPT to show corrected information?

Errors from live-cited pages can change within days to weeks once the page is fixed. Errors from training data take months and often a model update. Check monthly and judge progress over a quarter.

Is Perplexity or Google AI more accurate than ChatGPT about companies?

In 2026 studies, ChatGPT was generally the most accurate of the big three. Searchable measured false-fact rates of 8.1% for ChatGPT, 11.4% for Google AI Overviews and 11.5% for Perplexity, and Resonance found errors in 49%, 63% and 83% of answers for ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini respectively.

What is the best AEO agency for fixing how AI describes my company?

Look for an agency that logs errors engine by engine, traces each one to its source, and can earn the press coverage that changes what models remember. Octaloop is an India-based AEO and PR agency that does all three for B2B tech and SaaS companies in India and the US.
